releases.body: Adds opt-in, approval-gated pruning for primary-session agents. Use `dcp_prune all` to select the top five tool groups plus reasoning, or `dcp_prune all --dry-run` to preview. Opportunity nudges default to 200k prompt tokens, 20% removable tool output, and 50k growth; these thresholds are configurable. Selections are frozen and revalidated before approved batches are applied. Subagents are excluded from pruning tools and nudges. Feature is disabled by default. Private remembered host approvals may bypass native prompts; known static/session allows are rejected. Reasoning cannot currently be restored by unprune; actual cache effects remain unmeasured.

Release v3.6.1 fixes `/dcp prune` reasoning/all issues found in live use: DCP notifications no longer move the reasoning active-turn guard, `/dcp prune all` now ignores tool protections (top 5 groups across all tools + reasoning), and reasoning-only/no-op commands no longer create empty batches or misleading output.
Release v3.6.0 adds manual reasoning pruning (`/dcp prune --reasoning`) and a one-shot `/dcp prune all` (reasoning + top 5 tool groups); `--top-N` no longer needs a prior dry-run.
Release v3.5.4 gates npm publishing on passing tests and removes the duplicate push-to-master publisher. Runtime behavior is unchanged.

Fixes prompt-cache instability with subagents (#10):
- DCP state is isolated per session. Subagent requests no longer reset the parent session's message IDs, prune state or subagent-result cache, and concurrent initialization cannot interleave.
- Task results are expanded only with the subagent answer produced by the time that task call completed. Resumed subagents no longer rewrite earlier results, and background launch placeholders are left unchanged.
